abstract.title: Absolute music
abstract.text: Absolute music is music that is not explicitly "about" anything; in contrast to program music, it is non-representational.

acid jazz.title: Acid jazz
acid jazz.text: Acid jazz is a music genre that combines elements of funk, soul, and hip-hop.

acoustic.title: Acoustic music
acoustic.text: Acoustic music is music that solely or primarily uses instruments that produce sound through acoustic means, as opposed to electric or electronic means.

african.title: Music of Africa
african.text: The music of Africa is vast and highly diverse, with different regions and nations maintaining distinct musical traditions.

alt-pop.title: Alternative pop
alt-pop.text: Alternative pop is pop music with broad commercial appeal that is made by figures outside the mainstream, or which is considered more original, challenging, or eclectic than traditional pop music.

alternative rock.title: Alternative rock
alternative rock.text: Alternative rock is a category of rock music that evolved from the independent music underground of the 1970s.

ambient.title: Ambient music
ambient.text: Ambient music is a genre of music that emphasizes tone and atmosphere over traditional musical structure or rhythm. The genre evokes an "atmospheric", "visual", or "unobtrusive" quality.

art pop.title: Art pop
art pop.text: The genre draws on pop art's integration of high and low culture, and emphasizes imagery, style, and gesture over personal expression.

art rock.title: Art rock
art rock.text: Art rock is rock music that aims to distinguish the genre from popular entertainment, with the term typically being applied as the middle ground between mainstream and experimental rock.

avantgarde.title: Avant-garde music
avantgarde.text: Avant-garde music may be distinguished from experimental music by the way it adopts an extreme position within a certain tradition, whereas experimental music lies outside tradition.

bachata.title: Bachata (music)
bachata.text: Bachata is a genre of music that evolved in the Dominican Republic in the 20th century.

ballad.title: Sentimental ballad
ballad.text: Ballads are generally melodic enough to capture the listener's attention.

baroque.title: Baroque music
baroque.text: Baroque music refers to the period or dominant style of Western classical music composed from about 1600 to 1750.

bass music.title: Bass music
bass music.text: Bass music is any of several genres of electronic dance music and hip hop music arising from the 1980s on, focusing on a prominent bass drum and/or bassline sound.

beat.title: Beat music
beat.text: Beat music, British beat, or Merseybeat is a British popular music genre that developed around Liverpool in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

big beat.title: Big beat
big beat.text: Big beat is an electronic music genre that usually uses heavy breakbeats and synthesizer-generated loops and patterns – common to acid house/techno.

blues.title: Blues
blues.text: Blues is a music genre and musical form that originated among African Americans in the Deep South of the United States around the 1860s.

blues rock.title: Blues rock
blues rock.text: Blues rock is a fusion genre and form of rock and blues music that relies on the chords/scales and instrumental improvisation of blues.

bolero.title: Bolero
bolero.text: Bolero is a music genre which originated in eastern Cuba in the late 19th century as part of the trova tradition.

boogaloo.title: Boogaloo
boogaloo.text: Boogaloo or bugalú is a modern jazz genre of Latin music and dance which was popular in the United States in the 1960s.

breakcore.title: Breakcore
breakcore.text: Breakcore is a style of electronic dance music that emerged from jungle, hardcore, and drum & bass in the mid-to-late 1990s.

breaks.title: Break (music)
breaks.text: In popular music, a break is an instrumental or percussion section during a song derived from or related to stop-time – being a "break" from the main parts of the song or piece.

cha-cha.title: Cha-cha-chá (music)
cha-cha.text: Cha-cha-chá is a genre of Cuban music. It has been a popular dance music which developed from the danzón-mambo in the early 1950s, and became widely popular throughout the world.

chamber music.title: Chamber music
chamber music.text: Chamber music is a form of classical music that is composed for a small group of instruments—traditionally a group that could fit in a palace chamber or a large room.

chanson.title: Chanson
chanson.text: A chanson is generally any lyric-driven French song.

chicago blues.title: Chicago blues
chicago blues.text: Chicago blues is a form of blues music that developed in Chicago, Illinois. It is based on earlier blues idioms, such as Delta blues, but is performed in an urban style.

children's.title: Children's music
children's.text: Children's music or kids' music is music composed and performed for children. In European-influenced contexts this means music, usually songs, written specifically for a juvenile audience.

choral.title: Choir
choral.text: A choir, also known as a chorale or chorus, is a musical ensemble of singers.

christmas music.title: Christmas music
christmas music.text: Christmas music comprises a variety of genres of music regularly performed or heard around the Christmas season. Many songs simply have a winter or seasonal theme, or have been adopted into the canon for other reasons.

classic rock.title: Rock music
classic rock.text: It has its roots beginning as classic rock and roll, a style that drew from the African-American musical genres of blues and rhythm and blues, as well as from country music.

classical.title: Classical music
classical.text: Classical music is a tradition of art music in the Western world, considered to be distinct from Western folk music or popular music.

coldwave.title: Industrial metal
coldwave.text: Industrial metal is the fusion of heavy metal and industrial music, typically employing repeating metal guitar riffs, sampling, synthesizer or sequencer lines, and distorted vocals.

comedy.title: Comedy music
comedy.text: Comedy music or musical comedy is a genre of music that is comedic in nature.

concerto.title: Concerto
concerto.text: A concerto is, since the late Baroque era, mostly understood as an instrumental composition, written for one or more soloists accompanied by an orchestra or other ensemble.

contemporary.title: Contemporary music
contemporary.text: Contemporary music is whatever music is produced at the current time. Specifically, it could refer to:

country.title: Country music
country.text: Country music, also known as country and western or simply country, is a music genre originating from the United States. Once called hillbilly music, the term country music was popularized in the 1940s.

country rock.title: Country rock
country rock.text: Country rock is a music genre that fuses rock and country.

dancehall.title: Dancehall
dancehall.text: Dancehall is a genre of Jamaican popular music that originated in the late 1970s. Initially, dancehall was a more sparse version of reggae than the roots style, which had dominated much of the 1970s.

darkwave.title: Dark wave
darkwave.text: Dark wave is a music genre that emerged from the new wave and post-punk movement of the late 1970s.

deep house.title: Deep house
deep house.text: Deep house is a subgenre of house music that originated in the 1980s, initially fusing elements of Chicago house with the lush chords of 1980s jazz-funk and touches of soul music.

disco.title: Disco
disco.text: Disco is a genre of dance music and a subculture that emerged in the late 1960s from the United States' urban nightlife scene.

doo wop.title: Doo-wop
doo wop.text: Doo-wop is a subgenre of rhythm and blues music that originated in African-American communities during the late 1940s, mainly in the large cities of the United States.

downtempo.title: Downtempo
downtempo.text: Downtempo is a broad label for electronic music that features an atmospheric sound and slower beats than would typically be found in dance music.

dream pop.title: Dream pop
dream pop.text: Dream pop is a subgenre of alternative rock and neo-psychedelia that emphasizes atmosphere and sonic texture as strongly as it does pop melody.

drill.title: Drill music
drill.text: Drill music, also known as drill rap or simply drill, is a subgenre of hip-hop music with sonic origins in trap music and lyrical origins in gangsta rap. It began in Chicago, Illinois, United States, in the early 2010s.

drone.title: Drone music
drone.text: Drone music is a minimalist genre of music that emphasizes the use of sustained sounds, notes, or tone clusters called drones.

drum n bass.title: Drum and bass
drum n bass.text: Drum and bass, also known as drum 'n' bass, is a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the United Kingdom in the early 1990s.

dub.title: Dub music
dub.text: Dub is a musical style that grew out of reggae in the late 1960s and early 1970s. It is commonly considered a subgenre of reggae, though it has developed to extend beyond that style.

dub techno.title: Dub techno
dub techno.text: Dub techno is a subgenre of electronic music that originated in the early 1990s, blending the repetitive, minimal structures of techno with the echo-laden, spacey production techniques of dub music.

dubstep.title: Dubstep
dubstep.text: Dubstep is a genre of electronic dance music or Bass Music that originated in South London in the early 2000s.

easy listening.title: Easy listening
easy listening.text: Easy listening is a popular music genre and radio format that was most popular during the 1950s to the 1970s.

edm.title: Electronic dance music
edm.text: Electronic dance music, also referred to as dance music or club music, is a broad range of percussive electronic music genres originally made for nightclubs, raves, and festivals.

electro.title: Electro (music)
electro.text: Electro is a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the early 1980s. It is defined by the prominent use of the Roland TR-808 drum machine, and draws direct influence from early hip-hop and funk music.

electronic.title: Electronic music
electronic.text: Electronic music broadly is a group of music genres that employ electronic musical instruments, circuitry-based music technology and software, or general-purpose electronics in its creation.

ethereal.title: Ethereal wave
ethereal.text: Ethereal wave, also called ethereal darkwave, ethereal goth or simply ethereal, is a subgenre of dark wave music that is variously described as "gothic", "romantic", and "otherworldly".

experimental.title: Experimental music
experimental.text: Experimental music is a general label for any music or music genre that pushes existing boundaries and genre definitions.

favela funk.title: Funk carioca
favela funk.text: Funk carioca, also known as baile funk, Brazilian funk, or simply funk, is a Brazilian hip hop-influenced music genre from Rio de Janeiro, taking influences from musical styles such as Miami bass and freestyle.

field recording.title: Field recording
field recording.text: Field recording is the production of audio recordings outside recording studios, and the term applies to recordings of both natural and human-produced sounds.

folk.title: Folk music
folk.text: Folk music is a music genre that includes traditional folk music and the contemporary genre that evolved from the former during the 20th-century folk revival. Some types of folk music may be called world music.

folk rock.title: Folk rock
folk rock.text: Folk rock is a fusion genre of rock music with heavy influences from English and American folk music. It arose in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom in the mid-1960s.

folk, world, & country.title: Folk music
folk, world, & country.text: Folk music is a music genre that includes traditional folk music and the contemporary genre that evolved from the former during the 20th-century folk revival. Some types of folk music may be called world music.

footwork.title: Footwork (genre)
footwork.text: Footwork, also called juke, or Chicago juke, is a genre of electronic dance music derived from ghetto house with elements of hip-hop, first appearing in Chicago in the late 1990s.

free improvisation.title: Free improvisation
free improvisation.text: Free improvisation is a form of improvised music centered on a commitment to non-idiomatic musical expression.

funaná.title: Funaná
funaná.text: The funaná [funɐˈna] is a music and dance genre from Cape Verde. Funaná is an accordion-based music.

funk.title: Funk
funk.text: Funk typically consists of a complex percussive groove with rhythm instruments playing interlocking grooves that create a "hypnotic" and "danceable" feel.

funk / soul.title: Funk
funk / soul.text: Funk typically consists of a complex percussive groove with rhythm instruments playing interlocking grooves that create a "hypnotic" and "danceable" feel.

future jazz.title: Nu jazz
future jazz.text: Nu jazz is a genre of jazz and electronic music. The music blends jazz elements with other musical styles, such as funk, electronic music, and free improvisation.

garage house.title: Garage house
garage house.text: Garage house is an electronic dance music style that was developed alongside Chicago house music.

garage rock.title: Garage rock
garage rock.text: Garage rock is a raw and energetic style of rock and roll that flourished in the mid-1960s, most commonly in the United States and Canada, and has experienced a series of subsequent revivals.

ghetto.title: Ghetto house
ghetto.text: Ghetto house or booty house is a subgenre of house music which started being recognized as a distinct style from around 1992 onwards.

gospel.title: Gospel music
gospel.text: Gospel music is a traditional genre of Christian music and a cornerstone of Christian media, characterized by dominant vocals and lyrics that reflect Christian teachings and values.

hard bop.title: Hard bop
hard bop.text: Hard bop is a subgenre of jazz that is an extension of bebop.

hard house.title: UK hard house
hard house.text: UK hard house or simply hard house is a style of electronic dance music that emerged in the early 1990s and is synonymous with its association to the Trade club and the associated DJs there that created the style.

hard rock.title: Hard rock
hard rock.text: Hard rock or heavy rock is a heavier subgenre of rock music typified by vocals and electric guitars that are aggressive and distorted relative to traditional rock music.

hardcore hip-hop.title: Hardcore hip-hop
hardcore hip-hop.text: Hardcore hip-hop is a subgenre of hip-hop that developed through the East Coast hip-hop scene in the 1980s.

highlife.title: Highlife
highlife.text: Highlife is a Ghanaian music genre that originated along the coastal cities of present-day Ghana in the 19th century, during its history as a colony of the British and through its trade routes in coastal areas.

hip hop.title: Hip-hop
hip hop.text: Hip-hop is a genre of popular music that emerged in the early 1970s alongside an associated subculture in New York City.

horrorcore.title: Horrorcore
horrorcore.text: Horrorcore is a subgenre of hip-hop based on horror-themed and often darkly transgressive lyrical content and imagery.

house.title: House music
house.text: House music, or simply house, is a type of electronic dance music which is characterized by a repetitive four-on-the-floor beat and a typical tempo of 115–130 beats per minute.

idm.title: Intelligent dance music
idm.text: Intelligent dance music is a loose label used to describe experimental forms of electronic music associated with early-1990s ambient techno, "electronic listening music" and related forms of electronica.

illbient.title: Illbient
illbient.text: Illbient is a genre of electronic music and an art movement that originated among hip hop-influenced experimental musicians from New York City in the early 1990s.

indie pop.title: Indie pop
indie pop.text: Indie pop is a music genre and subculture that combines guitar pop with a DIY ethic in opposition to the style and tone of mainstream pop music.

indie rock.title: Indie rock
indie rock.text: Indie rock is a subgenre of rock music that originated in the United Kingdom, United States and New Zealand in the early to mid-1980s.

industrial.title: Industrial music
industrial.text: The term was coined in 1976 by Monte Cazazza and adopted by Throbbing Gristle with the founding of Industrial Records. Other early industrial musicians include NON and Cabaret Voltaire.

j-pop.title: J-pop
j-pop.text: J-pop is a form of popular music that entered the musical mainstream of Japan in the 1990s. In Japan it is known simply as pops.

jazz.title: Jazz
jazz.text: Jazz is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

jazz-funk.title: Jazz-funk
jazz-funk.text: Jazz-funk is a subgenre of jazz music characterized by a strong back beat, electrified sounds, and analog synthesizers. Similar genres to jazz-funk include acid jazz.

jump blues.title: Jump blues
jump blues.text: Jump blues is an uptempo style of blues with jazz and boogie woogie influence, usually played by small groups and featuring horn instruments.

jungle.title: Jungle music
jungle.text: Jungle is a genre of electronic music that developed in the 1990s out of the UK rave scene and Jamaican sound system culture.

krautrock.title: Krautrock
krautrock.text: Krautrock is a broad genre of experimental rock that developed in West Germany in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

latin.title: Latin music
latin.text: It may also include music from other territories where Spanish- and Portuguese-language music is made.

latin pop.title: Latin pop
latin pop.text: Latin pop, also referred to as Spanish-language pop or Portuguese-language pop, is a subgenre of popular music defined primarily as pop music performed in Spanish or Portuguese.

leftfield.title: Leftfield
leftfield.text: Leftfield are a British electronic music group formed in London in 1989, a duo of Neil Barnes and Paul Daley.

lo-fi.title: Lo-fi music
lo-fi.text: Low fidelity is a music or production quality in which elements usually regarded as imperfections in the context of a recording or performance are present, sometimes as a deliberate stylistic choice.

minimal.title: Minimal techno
minimal.text: Minimal techno is a subgenre of techno music. It is characterized by a stripped-down aesthetic that exploits the use of repetition and understated development.

modal.title: Mode (music)
modal.text: In music theory, the term mode or modus is used in a number of distinct senses, depending on context.

neo soul.title: Neo soul
neo soul.text: Neo soul is a genre of popular music. It has been noted by music writers for its conscious lyrics.

new age.title: New-age music
new age.text: New age is a genre of music intended to create artistic inspiration, relaxation, and optimism.

new wave.title: New wave music
new wave.text: New wave is a music genre encompassing pop-oriented styles that emerged in the United States and United Kingdom in the mid-to late 1970s.

no wave.title: No wave
no wave.text: No wave was an avant-garde music and visual art scene that emerged in the late 1970s in Downtown New York City. The term was coined as a rejection of commercial new wave music.

noise.title: Noise music
noise.text: Noise music is a subgenre of experimental music that is characterised by its use of unwanted noise as a primary musical element.

nu-disco.title: Nu-disco
nu-disco.text: Nu-disco is a 21st-century dance music genre associated with a renewed interest in the late 1970s disco, synthesizer-heavy 1980s European dance music styles, and early 1990s electronic dance music.

opera.title: Opera
opera.text: Opera is a form of Western theatre in which music is a fundamental component and dramatic roles are taken by singers.

orchestra.title: Orchestra
orchestra.text: An orchestra is a large instrumental ensemble typical of classical music or jazz, which combines instruments from different families. There are typically four main sections of instruments:

piano.title: Piano
piano.text: A piano is a keyboard instrument that produces sound when its keys are pressed, activating an action mechanism where hammers strike strings.

pop.title: Pop music
pop.text: Pop music, or simply pop, is a genre of popular music that originated in its modern form during the mid-1950s in the United States and the United Kingdom.

pop rap.title: Pop rap
pop rap.text: This genre gained mainstream popularity during the 1990s, though the influences and roots of pop rap can trace back to late-1980s hip-hop artists such as Run-DMC, LL Cool J, and Beastie Boys.

pop rock.title: Pop rock
pop rock.text: Pop rock is rock music with greater emphasis on professional songwriting and recording craft, and less emphasis on attitude than standard rock music.

post bop.title: Post-bop
post bop.text: Post-bop is a jazz term with several possible definitions and usages.

post-punk.title: Post-punk
post-punk.text: Post-punk is a loosely defined music genre and period that emerged in the late 1970s in the wake of punk rock.

power pop.title: Power pop
power pop.text: Power pop is a subgenre of rock music and a form of pop rock based on the early music of bands such as the Beach Boys, the Beatles, the Byrds, and the Who.

prog rock.title: Progressive rock
prog rock.text: Progressive rock is a broad genre of rock music that primarily developed in the United States and United Kingdom through the mid- to late 1960s.

psychedelic rock.title: Psychedelic rock
psychedelic rock.text: Psychedelic rock is a subgenre of rock music that originally emerged during the mid-1960s, inspired by psychedelic culture and centered primarily around the influence of psychoactive and hallucinogenic drugs.

punk.title: Punk rock
punk.text: Punk rock is a genre of rock music that emerged in the mid-1970s. Rooted in 1950s rock and roll and 1960s garage rock, punk bands rejected the overproduction and corporate nature of mainstream arena rock.

punta.title: Punta
punta.text: Punta is an Afro-indigenous dance and cultural music of the Belizean, Guatemalan, Honduran and Nicaraguan Garífuna people, originating from the Caribbean island of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

reggae.title: Reggae
reggae.text: Reggae is a music genre that originated in Jamaica in the late 1960s. The term also refers to the modern popular music of Jamaica and its diaspora.

rhythm & blues.title: Rhythm and blues
rhythm & blues.text: Rhythm and blues, frequently abbreviated as R&B or R'n'B, is a genre of popular music that originated within African American communities in the 1940s.

rhythmic noise.title: Power noise
rhythmic noise.text: Power noise is a subgenre of noise and post-industrial music, that originated predominantly in Europe during the 1990s. It draws primary influence from various styles of electronic dance music.

rock.title: Rock music
rock.text: It has its roots beginning as classic rock and roll, a style that drew from the African-American musical genres of blues and rhythm and blues, as well as from country music.

rock & roll.title: Rock and roll
rock & roll.text: Rock and roll is a genre of popular music that evolved in the United States during the late 1940s and early 1950s.

rocksteady.title: Rocksteady
rocksteady.text: Rocksteady is a music genre that originated in Jamaica around 1966. The term rocksteady comes from a popular dance style which is the subject in the Alton Ellis song "Rocksteady" and matched the new sound.

romantic.title: Romantic music
romantic.text: Romantic music is a stylistic movement in Western Classical music associated with the period of the 19th century commonly referred to as the Romantic era.

roots reggae.title: Roots reggae
roots reggae.text: It is identified with the life of the ghetto sufferer, and the rural poor.

shoegaze.title: Shoegaze
shoegaze.text: Shoegaze is a subgenre of indie and alternative rock characterised by ethereal soundscapes, obscured vocals, and extensive use of guitar effects and distortion. It was sometimes used interchangeably with "dream pop".

singer-songwriter.title: Singer-songwriter
singer-songwriter.text: A singer-songwriter is a musician who writes, composes, and performs their own musical material, including lyrics and melodies.

ska.title: Ska
ska.text: Ska is a music genre that originated in Jamaica in the late 1950s and was the precursor to rocksteady and reggae. It combined elements of Caribbean mento with American jazz and rhythm and blues.

soft rock.title: Soft rock
soft rock.text: Soft rock was prevalent on the radio throughout the 1970s and eventually metamorphosed into a form of the synthesized music of adult contemporary in the 1980s.

solo.title: Solo (music)
solo.text: Performing a solo is "to solo", and the performer is known as a soloist.

sonata.title: Sonata
sonata.text: In music, a sonata is a piece that consists of 3 or 4 movements that can be for different musical instruments.

soukous.title: Soukous
soukous.text: Soukous is a genre of dance music originating from the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo.

soul.title: Soul music
soul.text: Soul music is a popular music genre that originated in African-American communities throughout the United States in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

soul-jazz.title: Soul jazz
soul-jazz.text: Soul jazz or funky jazz is a subgenre of jazz that incorporates strong influences from hard bop, blues, soul, gospel and rhythm and blues.

string ensemble.title: String orchestra
string ensemble.text: A string orchestra is an orchestra consisting solely of a string section made up of the bowed strings used in Western Classical music.

symphony.title: Symphony
symphony.text: A symphony is an extended musical composition in Western classical music, most often for orchestra.

synth-pop.title: Synth-pop
synth-pop.text: Synth-pop is a music genre that first became prominent in the late 1970s and features the synthesizer as the dominant musical instrument.

tech house.title: Tech house
tech house.text: Tech house is a house music subgenre that prominently incorporates stylistic features from techno. Tech house originally featured the clean and minimal production style associated with techno from Detroit and the UK.

techno.title: Techno
techno.text: Techno is a genre of electronic music which is generally produced for use in a continuous DJ set, with tempos being in the range from 120 to 150 beats per minute.

trance.title: Trance music
trance.text: Trance is a genre of electronic dance music that emerged from the techno and EBM scene in Frankfurt, Germany, in the late 1980s and early 1990s, and quickly spread throughout Europe.

trap.title: Trap music
trap.text: Trap music, also known simply as trap, is a subgenre of hip-hop music that originated in the Southern United States. Lyrical references to trap began appearing in 1991, while the modern sound of trap emerged in 1999.

tribal house.title: Tribal house
tribal house.text: Tribal house is a subgenre of house music combined with world music rhythms. It is broadly characterized by elements of indigenous musical percussions.

trip hop.title: Trip hop
trip hop.text: Trip hop is a music genre defined as a psychedelic fusion of hip-hop and electronica with slow tempos and an atmospheric sound.

uk garage.title: UK garage
uk garage.text: UK garage, abbreviated as UKG, is a genre of electronic music which originated in England in the early to mid-1990s.

vocal.title: Vocal music
vocal.text: Vocal music is a type of singing performed by one or more singers, either with instrumental accompaniment or without instrumental accompaniment, in which singing provides the main focus of the piece.

world fusion.title: World music
world fusion.text: World music is an English phrase for styles of music from primarily non-English-speaking countries, including quasi-traditional, intercultural, and traditional music.

Agustín Barrios.title: Agustín Barrios
Agustín Barrios.text: Agustín Pío Barrios was a Paraguayan virtuoso classical guitarist and composer, regarded by some as one of the greatest performers and arguably the most prolific composer for the classical guitar.

Albert Marcœur.title: Albert Marcœur
Albert Marcœur.text: Albert Marcœur is a French composer, singer and songwriter. He began his career in the early 1970s.

Aleksi Perälä.title: Aleksi Perälä
Aleksi Perälä.text: Aleksi Perälä is a Finnish electronic music composer and producer. He has made music since 1988, and performed it live since 1996, switching between hardware and software over the years.

Alice Babs and her orchestra.title: Alice Babs
Alice Babs and her orchestra.text: Hildur Alice Nilson, known by her stage name Alice Babs, was a Swedish singer. She worked in a wide number of genres – Swedish folklore, Elizabethan songs and opera.

Alvin Curran.title: Alvin Curran
Alvin Curran.text: Alvin Curran is an American composer, performer, improviser, sound artist, and writer. He was born in Providence, Rhode Island, and lives and works in Rome, Italy.

Amy Winehouse.title: Amy Winehouse
Amy Winehouse.text: Amy Jade Winehouse was a British singer and songwriter.

Ann Peebles.title: Ann Peebles
Ann Peebles.text: Ann Lee Peebles is a retired American singer and songwriter who gained popularity for her Memphis soul albums of the 1970s while signed to Hi Records.

Annabel Lamb.title: Annabel Lamb
Annabel Lamb.text: Annabel Lamb is an English singer-songwriter. She has released eight albums beginning with her debut album, Once Bitten.

Björk.title: Björk
Björk.text: Björk Guðmundsdóttir is an Icelandic singer, songwriter, composer, record producer and actress. She is regarded as one of the most influential musicians of her era.

Bonde Do Role.title: Bonde do Rolê
Bonde Do Role.text: Bonde do Rolê was a Brazilian funk carioca-influenced electropop group from Curitiba, Paraná state, and consisted of MC's Pedro D'Eyrot, Laura Taylor, and DJ/MC Rodrigo Gorky.

Brenda Russell.title: Brenda Russell
Brenda Russell.text: Brenda Russell is an American-Canadian singer-songwriter, producer, and keyboardist. Russell has a diverse musical range which encompasses R&B, pop, soul, dance, and jazz.

Bruno Walter, Beethoven.title: Bruno Walter
Bruno Walter, Beethoven.text: Bruno Walter was a German-born conductor, pianist, and composer. Born in Berlin, he left Nazi Germany in 1933.

Carmen Villain.title: Carmen Villain
Carmen Villain.text: Carmen Maria Hillestad, known professionally as Carmen Villain, is a Norwegian-Mexican musical artist.

Carole King.title: Carole King
Carole King.text: Carole King Klein is an American singer-songwriter and musician renowned for her extensive contributions to popular music.

Chico Hamilton.title: Chico Hamilton
Chico Hamilton.text: Foreststorn "Chico" Hamilton was an American jazz drummer and bandleader. He came to prominence as sideman for Lester Young, Gerry Mulligan, Count Basie, and Lena Horne.

Crack Cloud.title: Crack Cloud
Crack Cloud.text: Crack Cloud are a Canadian musical and multimedia collective currently based in Calgary, Alberta, formed by drummer and frontman Zach Choy.

Craig Leon.title: Craig Leon
Craig Leon.text: Craig Leon is an American-born record producer, composer and arranger currently living in England.

Dana Gillespie.title: Dana Gillespie
Dana Gillespie.text: Richenda Antoinette de Winterstein Gillespie, known professionally as Dana Gillespie, is an English actress, singer and songwriter.

Darcy Clay.title: Darcy Clay
Darcy Clay.text: Darcy Clay was a New Zealand singer, songwriter and musician, who was made famous in 1997 for his Number 5 hit "Jesus I Was Evil", in which he recorded all of the instruments in his bedroom on a 4-track recorder.

Deee-Lite.title: Deee-Lite
Deee-Lite.text: Deee-Lite was an American house and dance music group formed in New York City.

Don Julian And The Meadowlarks.title: Don Julian (musician)
Don Julian And The Meadowlarks.text: Don Julian was an American rhythm and blues, funk and soul singer, guitarist and songwriter.

Earth, Wind & Fire.title: Earth, Wind & Fire
Earth, Wind & Fire.text: Earth, Wind & Fire is an American band formed in Chicago, Illinois, in 1969. Their music spans multiple genres, including jazz, R&B, soul, funk, disco, pop, Latin and Afro-pop.

Eivør.title: Eivør (singer)
Eivør.text: Eivør Pálsdóttir, known mononymously as Eivør, is a Faroese singer-songwriter. Born and raised in Syðrugøta, she had her first televised performance at the age of 13.

El Wali.title: El Wali (band)
El Wali.text: El Wali is a Western Saharan folk music group who recorded an album, Tiris, in 1994.

Errol Dunkley.title: Errol Dunkley
Errol Dunkley.text: Errol Dunkley, sometimes spelled Erroll Dunkley, is a Jamaican reggae musician, born in Kingston, Jamaica.

EsDeeKid, Rico Ace.title: EsDeeKid
EsDeeKid, Rico Ace.text: EsDeeKid is a British rapper from Liverpool, England. He released his debut mixtape, Rebel, in June 2025.

Eurythmics.title: Eurythmics
Eurythmics.text: Eurythmics were a British pop duo formed in 1980, consisting of the Scottish vocalist Annie Lennox and the English musician and producer Dave Stewart.

Eyedress.title: Eyedress
Eyedress.text: Idris Ennolandy Vicuña, known professionally as Eyedress, is a Filipino musician who has released albums in various rock, pop and electronic styles. Hailing from Manila, he currently lives in Los Angeles.

Fehlfarben.title: Fehlfarben
Fehlfarben.text: Fehlfarben is a Neue Deutsche Welle music band from Düsseldorf, Germany, that was formed in 1979.

Femtanyl.title: Femtanyl
Femtanyl.text: Femtanyl are a Canadian-American electronic music duo based in Toronto and Seattle consisting of founding member and lead singer Noelle Stockwood and multi-instrumentalist Juno Callender.

Frank de Wulf.title: Frank De Wulf
Frank de Wulf.text: Frank De Wulf is a Belgian DJ, musician and record label owner. He is considered one of the pioneers of the Belgian new beat and techno scene.

Fred Again.. & Bia.title: Fred Again
Fred Again.. & Bia.text: At the 66th Annual Grammy Awards, he was nominated for Best New Artist, won Best Dance/Electronic Album for his third album Actual Life 3, and won Best Dance/Electronic Recording for his 2023 single "Rumble".

Grace Barbé.title: Grace Barbé
Grace Barbé.text: Grace Barbé is a Seychellois-born Australian singer-songwriter who also performs with the Afrobeat and psychedelic band of the same name which includes Jamie Searle and Hardy Perrine.

Gro Anita Schønn.title: Gro Anita Schønn
Gro Anita Schønn.text: Gro Anita Schønn was a Norwegian singer.

Headless Chickens.title: Headless Chickens
Headless Chickens.text: The Headless Chickens was a New Zealand band.

Jacintha.title: Jacintha Abisheganaden
Jacintha.text: She is a founding member of the performance company TheatreWorks.

Jah Wobble.title: Jah Wobble
Jah Wobble.text: John Joseph Wardle is an English bass guitarist and singer. He was the original bass player in Public Image Ltd in the late 1970s and early 1980s; he left the band after two albums.

Jim Legxacy.title: Jim Legxacy
Jim Legxacy.text: James Folorunso Ifeanyi Olaloye known professionally as Jim Legxacy, is a British rapper, singer, and record producer from Catford, London Borough of Lewisham.

Jim Stafford.title: Jim Stafford
Jim Stafford.text: James Wayne Stafford is an American singer, songwriter, musician, and comedian. Stafford is self-taught on guitar, fiddle, piano, banjo, organ, and harmonica.

John Lennon.title: John Lennon
John Lennon.text: John Winston Ono Lennon was an English musician, songwriter and activist. He gained global fame as the founder, co-lead vocalist and rhythm guitarist of the Beatles.

José Feliciano.title: José Feliciano
José Feliciano.text: José Montserrate Feliciano García is a Puerto Rican musician. He recorded many international hits, including his rendition of the Doors' "Light My Fire" and his self-penned Christmas song "Feliz Navidad".

Judy Nylon, Crucial.title: Judy Nylon
Judy Nylon, Crucial.text: Judy Nylon is a multidisciplinary American artist who moved to London in 1970. She was half of the punk rock music group Snatch, which also featured fellow American immigrant Patti Palladin.

Junior Byles.title: Junior Byles
Junior Byles.text: Kenneth Byles, also known as "Junior Byles", "Chubby", or "King Chubby", was a foundation conscious roots reggae singer from Jamaica.

Larry Heard.title: Larry Heard
Larry Heard.text: Larry Heard is an American DJ, record producer, and musician who has recorded under various names, most notably Mr. Fingers.

Larry Heard & Mr. White.title: Larry Heard
Larry Heard & Mr. White.text: Larry Heard is an American DJ, record producer, and musician who has recorded under various names, most notably Mr. Fingers.

Lazar Berman, Liszt.title: Lazar Berman
Lazar Berman, Liszt.text: Lazar Naumovich Berman was a Soviet Russian classical pianist, Honoured Artist of the RSFSR.

Leoš Janáček, Wiener Philharmoniker, Sir.title: Leoš Janáček
Leoš Janáček, Wiener Philharmoniker, Sir.text: Leoš Janáček was a Czech composer, music theorist, folklorist, and teacher. He was inspired by Moravian and other Slavic music, including Eastern European folk music, to create an original, modern musical style.

Lloyd Clarke.title: Lloyd Clarke
Lloyd Clarke.text: Lloyd Clarke is a Jamaican ska musician. He had a series of hits in the early 1960s.

Lorez Alexandria.title: Lorez Alexandria
Lorez Alexandria.text: Lorez Alexandria was an American jazz singer, described as "one of the most gifted and underrated jazz singers of the twentieth century".

Los Thuthanaka.title: Los Thuthanaka
Los Thuthanaka.text: Los Thuthanaka is the debut studio album by the American duo Los Thuthanaka, consisting of siblings Chuquimamani-Condori and Joshua Chuquimia Crampton.

M'Pongo Love.title: M'Pongo Love
M'Pongo Love.text: Aimee Françoise M'Pongo Langu, known professionally as M'Pongo Love, was a Congolese singer and songwriter.

Maurice Williams & The Zodiacs.title: Maurice Williams and the Zodiacs
Maurice Williams & The Zodiacs.text: Maurice Williams and the Zodiacs were an American doo-wop/R&B vocal group in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

Mayumi Kojima.title: Mayumi Kojima
Mayumi Kojima.text: Mayumi Kojima is a Japanese Shibuya-kei musician. As of 2015, she has released 10 studio albums, 3 extended plays and several singles.

McCoy Tyner.title: McCoy Tyner
McCoy Tyner.text: Alfred McCoy Tyner was an American jazz pianist and composer known for his work with the John Coltrane Quartet from 1960 to 1965 and his long solo career afterward.

Michael Wycoff.title: Michael Wycoff
Michael Wycoff.text: Michael Wycoff was an American R&B singer. He scored several hits on the US R&B chart during the 1980s.

Mira Calix.title: Mira Calix
Mira Calix.text: Chantal Francesca Passamonte, known professionally as Mira Calix, was a South African-born British-based audio and visual artist and musician signed to Warp Records. She also worked as Warp's press officer.

Miriam Makeba.title: Miriam Makeba
Miriam Makeba.text: Zenzile Miriam Makeba, nicknamed Mama Africa, was a South African singer, songwriter, actress, and civil rights activist.

Nick Hakim.title: Nick Hakim
Nick Hakim.text: Nicolas Hakim is an American musician based in Queens, New York, United States. His first EP, Where Will We Go Part 1 & 2, was self-released in 2014.

Nolan Porter.title: Nolan Porter
Nolan Porter.text: Nolan Frederick Porter was an American R&B singer and songwriter who recorded two albums and six singles in the early 1970s. His best known song is "Keep On Keeping On", which became popular on the northern soul scene.

Odyssey.title: Odyssey (band)
Odyssey.text: Odyssey is a vocal trio originally from New York City, who are best known for their disco hits including "Native New Yorker", "Use It Up and Wear It Out", and "Going Back to My Roots".

Preoccupations.title: Preoccupations
Preoccupations.text: Preoccupations is a Canadian post-punk band from Calgary, Alberta, that formed in 2012 under the name Viet Cong.

Pretty Ugly.title: Pretty Ugly
Pretty Ugly.text: Pretty Ugly is the fourth studio album by the American punk rock band Lunachicks. It was released by Go-Kart Records in 1997.

Protomartyr.title: Protomartyr (band)
Protomartyr.text: Protomartyr is an American post-punk band formed in Detroit, Michigan, in 2010. The band consists of Joe Casey, Greg Ahee, Alex Leonard, and Scott Davidson.

Public Image Ltd..title: Public Image Ltd
Public Image Ltd..text: Public Image Ltd are an English post-punk band formed by lead vocalist John Lydon, guitarist Keith Levene, bassist Jah Wobble, and drummer Jim Walker in June 1978.

Radu Lupu, Franz Schubert.title: Radu Lupu
Radu Lupu, Franz Schubert.text: Radu Lupu was a Romanian pianist. He was widely recognized as one of the greatest pianists of his time.

Ramsey Lewis.title: Ramsey Lewis
Ramsey Lewis.text: Ramsey Emmanuel Lewis Jr. was an American jazz pianist, composer, and radio personality. Lewis recorded over 80 albums and received five gold records and three Grammy Awards in his career.

Ron Carroll.title: Ron Carroll
Ron Carroll.text: Ronald Michael Carroll was an American DJ, singer, songwriter, and music producer. He was primarily active on the house music circuit and openly gay.

SZA.title: SZA
SZA.text: Solána Imani Rowe, known professionally as SZA, is an American singer-songwriter.

Schubert, Budapest Philharmonic Orchestr.title: Franz Schubert
Schubert, Budapest Philharmonic Orchestr.text: Franz Peter Schubert was an Austrian composer of the late Classical and early Romantic eras.

Seu Jorge.title: Seu Jorge
Seu Jorge.text: Jorge Mário da Silva, known as Seu Jorge, is a Brazilian musician, singer, songwriter, and actor.

Single Gun Theory.title: Single Gun Theory
Single Gun Theory.text: Single Gun Theory was an Australian electronic dance music band formed in 1986.

Slowdive, Grouper.title: Slowdive
Slowdive, Grouper.text: Slowdive is an English rock band that formed in Reading, Berkshire, in 1989.

Sonique.title: Sonique (musician)
Sonique.text: Sonia Marina Clarke, better known by her stage name Sonique, is an English singer, musician and DJ.

Supertramp.title: Supertramp
Supertramp.text: Supertramp were a British rock band formed in London in 1970. Marked by the individual songwriting of founders Roger Hodgson and Rick Davies, the group were distinguished for blending progressive rock and pop styles.

Swans.title: Swans (band)
Swans.text: Swans are an American experimental rock band formed in 1981 by singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Michael Gira. Initially, their music was known for its sonic brutality and misanthropic lyrics.

T.I., Chris Brown.title: T.I.
T.I., Chris Brown.text: Clifford Joseph Harris Jr., known professionally as T.I. or Tip, is an American rapper and actor.

The Blues Busters.title: The Blues Busters
The Blues Busters.text: The Blues Busters was a vocal duo from Jamaica formed in 1960, consisting of Philip James and Lloyd Osbourne Campbell. The Blues Busters was the most consistently popular Jamaican male duo of the early 1960s.

The Earons.title: The Earons
The Earons.text: The Earons are a self-described "astro-funk" band from Tampa Bay, Florida. They were inspired by the cosmic mythology of Sun Ra with a bit of Anthony Braxton's mathematica.

The Jive Bombers.title: The Jive Bombers
The Jive Bombers.text: The Jive Bombers were an American R&B group from New York City.

The Monn Keys.title: The Monn Keys
The Monn Keys.text: The Monn Keys were a Norwegian musical show group that was active from 1948 until 1964. Founded by Sølvi Wang and Egil Monn-Iversen, the group became well-known in Norway for their jazz and pop music performances.

The Monotones.title: The Monotones
The Monotones.text: The Monotones were a six-member American doo-wop vocal group in the 1950s.

The Orioles.title: The Orioles
The Orioles.text: The Orioles were an American R&B group in the late 1940s and early 1950s. One of the first vocal groups in R&B, they were early pioneers of the doo-wop sound.

The Sundays.title: The Sundays
The Sundays.text: The Sundays were an English alternative rock band formed in Bristol in 1988. The band's lineup consisted of lead vocalist Harriet Wheeler, guitarist David Gavurin, bassist Paul Brindley, and drummer Patrick Hannan.

The Teenagers, Frankie Lymon.title: The Teenagers
The Teenagers, Frankie Lymon.text: The Teenagers were an American doo-wop music group, most noted for being one of rock music's earliest successes, presented to international audiences by DJ Alan Freed.

Theo Parrish.title: Theo Parrish
Theo Parrish.text: Theo Parrish is an American DJ and record producer based in Detroit, Michigan, and known for his genre-spanning DJ sets and unconventional house productions.

Throbbing Gristle.title: Throbbing Gristle
Throbbing Gristle.text: Throbbing Gristle were an English music and visual arts group formed in Kingston upon Hull by Genesis P-Orridge and Cosey Fanni Tutti, later joined by Peter "Sleazy" Christopherson and Chris Carter.

Trevor Dandy.title: Trevor Dandy
Trevor Dandy.text: Trevor Dandy is a Jamaican-born Canadian gospel and funk musician active in the 1970s.

Uranium Club.title: Uranium Club
Uranium Club.text: Uranium Club is an American punk rock band based in Minneapolis. The band consists of members Brendan Wells, Harry Wohl, Ian Stemper and Matt Stagner.

Vashti Bunyan.title: Vashti Bunyan
Vashti Bunyan.text: Jennifer Vashti Bunyan is an English singer-songwriter. She began her career in the mid-1960s and released a debut album, Just Another Diamond Day, in 1970.

Virna Lindt.title: Virna Lindt
Virna Lindt.text: Virna Lindt is a Swedish singer and record producer. Her debut single "Attention Stockholm" became an indie-chart hit in 1982.

Voyou.title: Voyou
Voyou.text: Thibaud Vanhooland, known professionally as Voyou, is a French singer-songwriter.
